front: Weight-only INT4 vs W8A8: which phase does each speed up?
back: Weight-only cuts bytes read, so it speeds bandwidth-bound decode. W8A8 or FP8 uses low-precision tensor cores, so it speeds compute-bound prefill.
A few hidden dimensions with values far larger than the rest, which appear in large models (LLM.int8() saw them from about 6.7B parameters). They wreck naive 8-bit activation quantization.
Divide each activation channel by a scale and multiply the matching weight row by it. The product is unchanged, but activations become easy to quantize.

Both are post-training 4-bit weight methods. GPTQ compensates rounding error column by column using second-order information; AWQ protects salient channels found from activation magnitudes with per-channel scaling.

front: Llama 2 70B weights in fp16, INT8, INT4 (group 128)?
back: About 140 GB, 70 GB and 36 GB (4 bits plus one fp16 scale per 128 weights ≈ 4.125 bits).

front: Why is perplexity not enough to approve a quantized model?
back: It is an average. Losses concentrate in maths, code, long context and rarer languages, so use task-sliced evals against the fp16 baseline.
Writing and re-reading the N × N score and probability matrices in HBM. It tiles Q, K, V into SRAM and uses an online softmax.
Keep a running max and running sum per row; when a new tile raises the max, rescale the accumulated output by e^(m_old − m_new). Exact, tile by tile.

front: MHA vs GQA vs MQA KV per token for Llama 2 70B's shape?
back: 64 KV heads: 2.5 MiB. 8 (GQA, as published): 320 KiB. 1 (MQA): 40 KiB. All fp16.
MQA saves the most cache but loses more quality and trains less stably; GQA keeps most of the saving with quality close to MHA.
SGLang keeps finished requests' KV in a radix tree keyed by tokens, reuses the longest matching prefix, evicts leaves LRU and schedules longest-prefix-first.

front: Why can prefix KV be shared at all?
back: With causal attention a token's keys and values depend only on earlier tokens, so identical prefixes produce identical KV.
Sarathi-Serve's term for decoding sequences freezing while a whole long prompt is prefilled in one iteration.
Smaller chunks give tighter tail TPOT for everyone; the long request pays a higher TTFT and re-reads earlier chunks' KV.
Prompt tokens × KV bytes per token ÷ link bandwidth. 4,000 × 320 KiB ≈ 1.31 GB at 50 GB/s ≈ 26 ms, overlapped layer by layer.
Decode barely uses compute, so the decode pool can run on cheaper or older machines while prefill gets compute-dense ones.

front: When does KV offload beat recompute?
back: When reload time (bytes ÷ host or network bandwidth) is less than prefill time for those tokens: long prefixes, big models.
Small-batch decode launches hundreds of short kernels; graphs replay the whole sequence with one launch. Shapes must be fixed, so engines capture several batch sizes and pad.
